# Evening one: draw the fall

About 20 minutes, chart beside you.

1. **Set up.** In Blender, start a file from the **2D Animation** template. Set the [frame rate](asset:blender_format) to 24 in Output Properties > Format, and type 24 in the timeline's End box.
2. **Draw a floor line** near the bottom and a mark for 10 near the top, on the **Fills** layer (Object Data properties > Layers), so they stay on every frame. Then click **Lines** and draw every ball there. Heights measure the **bottom of the ball**: at 0 it sits on the floor.
3. **Each drawing goes two frames after the last:** drawing 1 on frame 1, drawing 2 on frame 3, and drawing 6, the first contact, on frame 11. Frame 6 shows drawing 3, not the contact.
4. **Draw drawings 1 to 6** at your chart's heights. Drawing 6 touches the floor.

![From chart to timeline: chart frame 1 becomes timeline frame 1, chart frame 6 becomes timeline frame 11, chart frame 12 becomes timeline frame 23](asset:chart_to_timeline)

{{deeper}}

**Only 5 minutes?** Draw just drawings 1 and 6. Fill in the rest another night.

**In Harmony,** create a scene at 24 frames per second; the steps are the same.

**No tool working yet?** Draw each ball on its own small sheet of paper, with the floor in the same place. A phone video of you flipping through them counts.
